quote: Noodles are wheat-based (the dry tantanmen uses thin Kagawa wheat noodles), and the kitchen runs Sichuan/Chinese dishes with soy-based sauces and fried items, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent.
found: 「汁なし担々麵 1,320円 … 香川県産の細いうどんに四川の唐辛子と山椒の香りが絡みあう。」 and 「メニューは前菜系から点心、炒め物、丼、麺など豊富なラインナップ。」 plus 「焼きぎょうざ 5個 550円 … 柔らかい皮に包まれ味わい深い。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page; trading status cross-checked on s.tabelog.com/kyoto/A2601/A260203/26003254/ with an iPhone UA (200, live, 四川料理/中華料理, no 閉店 banner)
note: Correct: 香川県産の細いうどん is literally Kagawa wheat udon, so the 汁なし担々麺 line is verbatim. Two strengthenings worth making: the page also lists 焼きぎょうざ with 「柔らかい皮」 (wheat gyoza wrappers) and 点心 as a whole menu category, which are firmer wheat vectors than the inferred 'fried items'. 'Soy-based sauces' is inference — the page says 甘辛極旨タレ / 旨タレ, never 醤油; keep the claim but stop attributing the soy wording to this source.

quote: Menu is meat-forward (glazed pork, beef mapo tofu, chicken, pork tantanmen); no vegan dishes or separated plant-based prep were documented.
found: 「てりどんきんし地獄盛り … 錦糸玉子の上に旨タレが絡む豚肉がたっぷりと。」「牛肉麻婆豆腐 1,760円 … ぷりっと豆腐と牛肉」「軍鶏のよだれ鶏 ハーフ 1,100円」. The 汁なし担々麵 entry describes only 「香川県産の細いうどんに四川の唐辛子と山椒の香りが絡みあう」 — no pork is named.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Meat-forward is well supported, but 'pork tantanmen' is not on this page — the tantanmen description names noodles and Sichuan chilli/sansho only. Also the page's own text adds 錦糸玉子 (shredded egg) on the signature てりどん, a non-vegan item the record misses. Swap 'pork tantanmen' for 'egg-topped signature teridon'.

quote: The broth is described as a pork-bone base seasoned with a deeply flavored soy sauce (shoyu), which in this style is virtually always wheat-containing.
found: 「50年以上続く京都の有名老舗ラーメン店からのれん分け。豚骨ベースで深みのある醤油・たっぷりの野菜スープなので後味もさっぱり！」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page; trading status cross-checked on s.tabelog.com/kyoto/A2601/A260401/26013188/ (200, live, 3.36 / 98 reviews, no 閉店 banner)
note: Verbatim: 豚骨ベースで深みのある醤油. The wheat inference on brewed shoyu is the record's own and is standard; the page states no ingredients. Worth adding the far more direct wheat vectors this same page lists: 餃子 250円, 半チャーハンセット and 焼めし/焼飯 (fried rice cooked with the same shoyu), and a whole 定食 range built on them.

quote: Broth is a pork-bone (tonkotsu) base and bowls are topped with roast pork, so animal products are integral to the dishes.
found: 「豚骨ベースで…」 plus the menu: 「チャーシューメン 800円」「焼豚 大 650円 / 小 400円」「ターロー（大）1,000円」「特上 焼肉丼 500円」「豚キムチ 420円」「焼豚定食（ミニラーメン・ライス・焼豚・漬物）980円」.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Supported and then some — pork appears in the broth, the chashu, the ターロー, the 焼肉丼 and seven of the nine 定食. The only near-vegan item on the page is もやし炒め定食, and it is served with the ramen, so do not soften this one.

quote: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and bowls use a soy-sauce-based tare; no gluten-free handling is offered.
found: 「創業は1983年、創業以来約40年間“豚骨醤油”一筋」「メニューはシンプルでラーメンの味は“豚骨醤油”１種類、サイズは並と大、チャーシュー麵（並・大）のみ。サイドメニューは、焼きめしの並と大、キムチ、メンマ、ライスのみです。」「中細麺がスープによく絡まります。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited Kyoto City Tourism Association page; venue identity confirmed via Ecosia (tabelog 26003217, 京都府京都市伏見区京町大黒町118, 桃山御陵前) against the article's 京町大黒町1185; trading confirmed live on s.tabelog.com (200, 3.53, no 閉店)
note: Right venue despite the name inversion — the article calls it 「ラーメン大黒伏見本店」 while the shop's own site and Tabelog say 「大黒ラーメン 本店」; same address block, so this is not a sibling-branch citation. The wheat noodles and the 豚骨醤油 tare are on the page. But 'boiled in shared water' and 'no gluten-free handling is offered' are NOT — the article never mentions either, and a tourism blog is not where an absence-of-GF-handling claim can be evidenced. Rephrase the first as an inference and re-source the second. Also add 焼きめし: the page says nearly 100% of customers order the fried rice alongside, i.e. a shoyu-seasoned wok in constant use.

quote: The broth is a tonkotsu-shoyu (pork-bone soy sauce) base; the shoyu tare in this style is virtually always wheat-containing.
found: 「伏見桃山で豚骨醤油味のラーメンと言えば真っ先に思い浮かぶのが「ラーメン大黒伏見本店」…創業以来約40年間“豚骨醤油”一筋」 and 「黄金色のスープは豚骨と鶏ガラをベースにじっくりと丁寧に煮込こまれ」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Verbatim 豚骨醤油, stated three times including as the shop's single flavour for 40 years. The wheat-in-brewed-shoyu step is the record's own standard inference; the page states no ingredients. Solid as written.

quote: Broth is simmered from pork and chicken bones and bowls are topped with char siu pork; there are no vegan items and no separate preparation.
found: 「黄金色のスープは豚骨と鶏ガラをベースにじっくりと丁寧に煮込こまれおり」「チャーシューは薄切りでモモ肉とバラ肉が適度に混じっている、京都スタイルのチャーシュー。」「焼きめしの具材は細かく刻んだチャーシュー、玉子、ネギと至ってシンプル。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Fully supported and understated. The page also shows the only side dish is 焼きめし, and it contains both chashu and 玉子 (egg) — so the fried rice is not a vegan fallback either. The genuinely animal-free items on the whole menu are キムチ, メンマ and ライス. Worth naming that explicitly so a vegan reader is not left guessing.

quote: The house-made noodles are cut from domestic wheat (and egg) in-house, so flour is handled on-site; a shared-kitchen wheat environment should be assumed.
found: 「黄金色の麺は国産小麦と卵のみを使用した、約1mm四方の自家製麺。打ち粉に北海道産とうもろこし粉を使うなど、こだわり抜かれた超贅沢な一杯。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page; venue and trading cross-checked on s.tabelog.com/kyoto/A2601/A260303/26035446/ (200, live, 53 reviews, no 閉店)
note: Verbatim 国産小麦と卵のみ + 自家製麺, so on-site flour handling is established. Two things to fold in, in opposite directions. (a) LOOK-BOTH-WAYS: the 打ち粉 (dusting flour) is 北海道産とうもろこし粉 — CORN, not wheat. That is the one place a reader would expect airborne wheat flour and it is not wheat here; the record should say so rather than let 'flour is handled on-site' imply a wheat-dusted bench. (b) Tabelog records the former shop name as 「Odashi&Wheat isao」 — the wheat identity is in the shop's own history, worth a line.

quote: The signature dashi bowl uses no soy sauce at all — it is seasoned with about 1 gram of Iwate salt only — so the usual wheat-shoyu tare risk is absent from the broth (the wheat comes from the noodles instead).
found: 「朝限定の「oだしのニューめん」は、利尻昆布、さわら、まぐろ節で出汁を引き、味付けは岩手県「のだ塩」1ｇのみとシンプルに。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Verbatim, including the 1g and the Iwate (岩手県「のだ塩」) provenance — a rare, genuinely useful GF-positive line and exactly the kind of finding this sweep should not lose. One scope caveat: the page attributes the salt-only seasoning to the 朝限定 「oだしのニューめん」 specifically, not to every dish, so word it as 'the morning-only signature bowl'.

quote: The dashi is animal-based throughout (sawara/Spanish mackerel and bonito alongside kombu), and the noodles contain egg, so there is no clean vegan or vegetarian path.
found: 「利尻昆布、さわら、まぐろ節で出汁を引き」 — Rishiri kombu, sawara and まぐろ節 (dried TUNA flakes). Noodles: 「国産小麦と卵のみを使用した…自家製麺」.
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: Substance is right — fish dashi plus egg noodles, so no vegan and no ovo-free vegetarian path — but the fish is misnamed: the page says まぐろ節 (tuna), not かつお節 (bonito). Change 'bonito' to 'dried tuna flakes'. It matters to anyone avoiding a specific fish, and it is the same class of slip as a mistranslated ingredient.

quote: Because the owner makes and explains the dashi in front of guests, it is easy to ask exactly what is in the bowl, and the seasoning is unusually transparent: kombu, sawara, bonito, salt, and house wheat-and-egg noodles.
found: 「料理や小売り、情報発信を通して「出汁を知ってもらいたい」と昨年6月オープン。店主・井上さんが出汁を引く様子を見て、味わって、話を聞けば自然と出汁が身近に感じられる。」
method: 1 plain fetch of the cited page
note: The owner-explains-the-dashi positive is verbatim (店主・井上さん, watch it being drawn, ask questions) and is the strongest asset this record has for an allergy-aware diner — keep it. Same correction as above: 'bonito' must read 'dried tuna (まぐろ節)'.
